app.description: Convert exchange CSV history to rotki's import format. Everything runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
app.name: rotki migration assistant

blocker.no_date_match: No date in the sample matches this format.
blocker.no_file: Choose a CSV file with at least two columns.

convert.description: Convert the whole file and download the result.
convert.title: Convert

file.description: Pick the CSV your exchange exported.
file.title: Choose file

formats.description: Check how the export writes dates and decimals.
formats.title: Dates and numbers

mapping.description: Tell the converter where each value rotki needs comes from.
mapping.title: Map columns

preview.description: See what rotki will import from the first rows.
preview.title: Preview

fallback.custom: The recipe gives this field {count} other source to try when it is empty. | The recipe gives this field {count} other sources to try when it is empty.
fallback.label: If empty, use
fallback.type_by_side: When empty, use Deposit for rows that receive and Withdrawal for rows that send

help.description: A note shown in rotki, such as an order or transaction id.
help.fee: A zero or empty fee is left out.
help.fee_currency: The asset the fee was paid in. Needed when there is a fee.
help.location: The exchange or place these rows come from.
help.receive_amount: How much of it was received.
help.receive_currency: The asset received. On a buy of BTC/EUR, that is BTC.
help.spend_amount: How much of it was given up.
help.spend_currency: The asset given up. On a buy of BTC/EUR, that is EUR.
help.timestamp: When it happened. The date format is set in the next step.
help.type: What kind of event each row is. Map every value the export uses below.

field_mapping.location_external: rotki will list these rows under External. Pick the exchange if it is in the list.
field_mapping.split: Take one part of the value

footer.privacy: Your files never leave this page. It has no server to send them to, and its content security policy blocks every network request.

any_export.description: Pick which column holds what, step by step. Save the mapping and reuse it when the exchange moves its columns around.
any_export.title: Any exchange export

large_files.description: Rows stream from your disk and the result goes back to it, so memory does not grow with the file. A 1 GB export converts in under a minute and a half.
large_files.title: Large files welcome

on_device.description: Files are read and converted inside this tab. Nothing is uploaded, and the page is not allowed to make network requests.
on_device.title: Stays on your device

index_page.heading: Bring your exchange history into rotki
index_page.intro: Turn a CSV export from any exchange into rotki's generic trades or events format, ready for {menu} in rotki.
index_page.native_importers: Some exports need no conversion: rotki reads exports from Binance, CoinTracking, Kucoin, Nexo and several other services as they are. Choose your file anyway and the first step tells you when rotki can import it directly.
index_page.title: Convert exchange history for rotki

verify.body: Open your browser's developer tools on the Network tab while you convert a file: no request goes out. The page ships a content security policy with {policy}, so the browser would block one even if the code tried. The footer links the release, the exact commit and the build that produced this deployment, and each release carries a copy of the site with a build attestation you can verify.
verify.heading: Check it yourself

messages.amount_negative: {column} "{value}" is negative; turn on "Ignore the sign" for it.
messages.amount_not_number: {column} "{value}" is not a number with "{separator}" as the decimal separator.
messages.missing_column: The file has no column named "{column}".
messages.needs_route: Say which rows are trades: pick the columns a trade fills.
messages.needs_source: {column} needs a source column or a fixed value.
messages.no_dates: The recipe has no valid date format or time zone.
messages.no_decimal_separator: The recipe has no valid decimal separator.
messages.no_format: The recipe names no rotki format.
messages.no_header: The file ended before its header row.
messages.no_input: The recipe has no valid encoding, delimiter or header row.
messages.no_storage: This browser does not let the page store the converted file. Private windows often block it; open the page in a normal window and try again.
messages.not_recipe: The file is not a migration assistant recipe.
messages.request_invalid_output: The conversion request names invalid output files.
messages.request_invalid_texts: The conversion request carries no texts for the rejected rows.
messages.request_no_file: The conversion request carries no file.
messages.request_not_object: The conversion request is not an object.
messages.request_unknown_type: The conversion request has an unknown type.
messages.timestamp_format: Timestamp "{value}" does not match the date format {format}.
messages.unknown_location: Location "{value}" is not a rotki location.
messages.unknown_time_zone: This browser does not know the time zone "{timeZone}".
messages.unknown_type: Type "{value}" is not a rotki event type; map it to one or skip it.

expectation.converted: {converted} of {total} row converts | {converted} of {total} rows convert

step_convert.import_help: In rotki, open {import_data}, pick {custom_import}, then {import_format}, and choose {file}.
step_convert.large_file: A large file converts best in a normal window: private windows keep the result in memory instead of on disk.
step_convert.recipe_note: Next time this exchange exports, the saved recipe sets every step up for you.
step_convert.rejected_help: The rejected file lists each row with the reason in its last column.

encoding.hint: Change it if letters such as ü or é look garbled.
encoding.label: Encoding

help.any_csv: Any CSV works: the next steps detect its layout and let you say what each column holds.
help.where: Most exchanges put the export under {history}, {statements} or {reports}, as CSV. Pick the full history if the exchange offers a choice.

native_importer.body: This is the format of rotki's {importer} importer, so it needs no conversion. In rotki, open {location} and choose this file. You can still convert it here if you want to change how it is read.
native_importer.title: rotki imports this file directly

your_file.description: The highlighted row holds the column names. If the exchange wrote other lines above them, click the right row.
your_file.partial: Settings and previews use the first record of {size}. | Settings and previews use the first {count} records of {size}.
your_file.title: Your file

ambiguous.description: The sample fits {count} format that reads the dates differently. Pick the one your exchange uses. | The sample fits {count} formats that read the dates differently, for example day-first and month-first. Pick the one your exchange uses.
ambiguous.title: Check the day and month order

hint.matches_all: Matches every date in the sample.
hint.none: No format matches the dates in the sample.

pattern.hint: Tokens: YYYY MM M DD D HH H hh h mm ss SSS A MMM. Put words in brackets, as [at]. Anything else must match as written.
pattern.label: Pattern

time_zone.hint: Used when a date carries no offset. Many exchanges export in UTC.
time_zone.label: Time zone of the export

unreadable.number: not a number with this separator

step_mapping.matched_by_name: Columns are matched by name, so a saved recipe still works when the exchange moves them around.

route.counts: In the sample: {trades} as trades, {events} as events.
route.custom: The recipe makes a row a trade when {rule}.
route.explanation: A row that fills both columns, as a sent and a received amount, becomes a trade. Any other row becomes a deposit, withdrawal or other event.
route.first_column: A row is a trade when
route.title: Trades and events

swap.explanation: Map the columns above as they read for a buy. On a sell, what was spent and what was received are swapped.
swap.title: Buys and sells

step_preview.first_rows_of_file: First row of the file: | First {count} rows of the file:

rejected.description: These rows would go to a separate file. Fix the cause to bring them in, or leave them out. Row numbers match the file table in the first step.
rejected.title: Rejected rows

both.description: Each row sends, receives or swaps, as in exports from Koinly, CoinTracker or ZenLedger. Swaps become trades, the rest events.
both.example: Sent 1 ETH, received 3,000 USDC; received 0.01 ETH
both.title: Both, from one file

events.description: Each row moves one asset: deposits, withdrawals, staking rewards, income, losses.
events.example: Received 0.01 ETH as a staking reward
events.title: Events

trades.description: Each row swaps one asset for another: buys, sells, conversions.
trades.title: Trades

step_target.label: rotki format
step_target.separate_files: rotki imports trades and events from separate files. If your export mixes both, choose Both: you get one file of each to import.

value_map.empty: No values in the sample yet.
value_map.in_sample: {n} row in the sample | {n} rows in the sample
value_map.unmapped: {values} not mapped yet, so {rows} of the sample would be rejected. Pick a type, or skip them if rotki should not import them.
